messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — I ran a mixed Nsight Systems + nvprof sweep on an 8x A100 TP+PP run. Seeing ~18-22% idle on some ranks during KV-cache warmup and a bursty all-reduce tail on others. Uploading traces now.

maya: Timeline shows repeated small gaps (~150-300us) aligned with KV merge calls, looks like frequent microbatches are triggering extra synchronizations.

tom: Can you paste the Nsight command and the small timeline snippet? think we saw a similar microburst last month. :thinking_face:

maya: nsight command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=1975004321_run --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu ./profile_tp_pp.sh
```
And a trimmed timeline (nsys export -> CSV) shows NVTX markers: KVCACHE_FETCH / KV_MERGE / ALLREDUCE_START / ALLREDUCE_END repeated rapidly.

sanjay: I added micro-timers around kv_merge and allreduce in runtime. sample logs: 
```
[1975004321.101] rank0 kv_merge start
[1975004321.102] rank0 allreduce start
[1975004321.103] rank0 allreduce end (185us)
[1975004321.103] rank0 kv_merge end (42us)
[1975004321.110] rank1 kv_merge start
[1975004321.111] rank1 allreduce start
[1975004321.112] rank1 allreduce end (240us)
```
So timing varies a lot across ranks.

lauren: Hypothesis: batching heuristic + prefetch cause frequent tiny accumulations, which force allreduce on many small tensors. If the kernel selector picks a suboptimal matmul/transpose kernel for short sequences, we lose overlap.

anshul: I can force kernel-selector to prefer the high-throughput matmul for these shapes and re-run. Also will augment the profiler with our comm/compute overlap counters (added last sprint).

maya: Nice — also try increasing the batching accumulation window to 6ms and disable kv prefetch for a run. Want to see if that smooths bursts.

tom: If you re-run, add this nvprof-like capture snippet for per-kernel timing: 
```
nvprof --print-gpu-trace --log-file nvprof_1975004321.log ./run_profile.sh
```
We should extract kernel names + elapsed cycles and align with NVTX.

ci-bot: Upload complete: s3://redwood-profiles/1975004321/nsys.zip and s3://redwood-profiles/1975004321/nvprof.log :white_check_mark:

maya: I also exported a flamegraph from perf metrics — shows a cluster of short allreduce ops that dominate tail time on rank 3 and 5.

sanjay: For instrumentation, I'll add an event-id on KV ops so we can correlate same logical KV merge across ranks in the timeline. That should tell us if skew is due to imbalance or network scheduling.

lauren: Small suggestion — add a soft coalescing layer where we merge small tensors for allreduce if total bytes < 64KB. Might significantly reduce handshake overhead. Worth A/B.

anshul: Running two A/Bs now: (A) kernel-selector=fast-matmul + accumulate-window=6ms, (B) kernel-selector=default + kv-prefetch=off + coalescing enabled. Will share profiles.

maya: Created PERF-987 and linked traces. Assigning to eng-runtime perf squad. If either hypothesis fixes >10% tail, we can land default changes behind a flag.

tom: Great. If A wins, we should also update the kernel selection cost table for short-seq shapes so it's not fooled by latency heuristics.

maya: Agreed. Thanks all — will post results here when runs finish. :rocket:
